newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria to open stock exchange this year.
newsitem.headline: Algeria to open stock exchange this year.

text.p: Algeria plans to start up a stock exchange this year in line with its programme to privatise many state-owned firms and set up a market-driven economy, the finance minister said.
The start of the Algerian bourse would mark the first time stocks are traded in the former French colony since Algeria won its independence in 1962.

"There will be a bourse that will start listing some companies and we will likely achieve many privatisation operations through the exchange market here," Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui told Reuters in an interview this week.
Algeria expects to sell more than 250 state-owned firms this year under its privatisation programme that got new vigour from a recent law stripping away some of the impediments to would-be investors.

The changes to the landmark 1995 law included repealing the measures requiring new owners to retain all workers and keep the company's activities unchanged for five years. Instead, the law now offers incentives like tax breaks and easy loans to investors who save jobs and upgrade the firms.
Bankers are undergoing special training courses in Algeria and abroad to familiarise themselves with the working of a stock market, Harchaoui said.
The creation of the bourse is part of a broad programme to retool the banking and financial system to meet the needs of economic liberalisation.
Other government officials have said privatisation would get a boost with the June 5 parliamentary elections.

Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. Since then about 60,000 people have died in violence between Islamist rebels and government forces.

The government plans to offer up soon to investors -- including foreigners -- the state-owned Banque de Development Local (BDL). One reason is that BDL's business portfolio is dominated by private companies.

Algeria is also preparing to open a treasury bills secondary market. At first only banks, insurance and other financial institutions will be allowed to deal in this market before brokers are registered, Harchaoui said.
As part of the economic liberalisation, Algeria has finalised a programme to transform the banking system and expand links with the insurance industry.
Insurance has been the country's main savings route because of the mandatory insurance system.
